summary: Obfuscated preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes opaque bundled payload
details: @servicetitan/hammer-token@3.1.3 ships a heavily obfuscated preinstall script (`setup.mjs`, `node setup.mjs` declared as the preinstall hook) that downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...zip` and then uses the downloaded Bun binary via `execFileSync` to run a sibling 727KB obfuscated file `math_init.js` at install time. `setup.mjs` uses `_0xNNNNNN` hex identifiers, string-lookup indirection objects (`YCZJE: function(a,b,c,d){return a(b,c,d);}`), and wrapper functions over `https.get` and `execFileSync` to hide the fetch and exec. `math_init.js` is a Bun-compiled bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) with a rotating string-array constant table (`WV8StW`), single-letter identifiers, and hex-encoded literals; it is not the advertised design-token functionality and can only be executed through the freshly downloaded alternate runtime. A separate module `src/utils/figma/get-token.js` also references `child_process`, `fs`, `http`, `process.env`, `process.platform`, and a `POST fetch(...)` alongside Figma endpoints, consistent with additional host/network-reaching code paths. A design-token package has no legitimate need to install a second language runtime and hand it opaque bytes at install time; the obfuscation, alternate-runtime fetch, and opaque bundle together form the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern executed automatically on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
